skill.name: memory-systems
skill.description: Design layered memory architectures for agents using vector stores, property graphs, temporal relationships, retrieval, and consolidation patterns.
skill.summary: Build agent memory systems that preserve entities, relationships, and time-aware facts across sessions.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: All 30 static findings are false positives caused by graph identifiers, temporal queries, comments, or Markdown code fences. No shell execution or system reconnaissance is present. One medium-risk design issue remains because retrieved memory content enters agent context without an explicit trust boundary.

remediation.issue: Retrieved memory content is concatenated into agent context without trust labels or instruction filtering.
remediation.suggestion: Treat memories as untrusted data, preserve source metadata, delimit retrieved content, reject embedded instructions, and require authorization before storing sensitive facts.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Memory Content Enters Agent Context
semantic_findings.description: The reference retrieves stored memories, formats their content as text, and concatenates it into the active context without trust labels or instruction filtering. An attacker who can influence stored memory could persist indirect prompt-injection instructions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example directly concatenates retrieved memory content into context with no visible trust boundary. Exploitation depends on an attacker gaining influence over stored memories.

content.value_statement: Agents lose useful state when context expires and simple retrieval cannot preserve relationships or historical validity. This skill guides layered memory design using vector, graph, temporal, and consolidation patterns.
actual_capabilities: Compares working, short-term, long-term, entity, and temporal memory layers.
Guides selection among file storage, vector retrieval, knowledge graphs, and temporal graphs.
Provides Python examples for vector search, property graphs, temporal relationships, and entity retrieval.
Explains semantic, entity-based, and time-aware memory retrieval patterns.
Describes consolidation, context integration, retention, backup, and monitoring considerations.
limitations: The vector examples use deterministic or random placeholder embeddings instead of a production model.
The provided stores are in-memory examples without production persistence, authentication, encryption, or access control.
The integrated script leaves memory consolidation unimplemented.
Production deployments still require storage selection, privacy controls, evaluation, and operational monitoring.

output_examples.input: Choose memory for a support agent that must remember preferences but has simple queries.
output: Recommended architecture: session memory plus a long-term vector store with user and timestamp metadata.
Retrieve by semantic similarity and user identifier before relevant conversations.
Add retention limits, consent records, deletion controls, and periodic quality checks.

output_examples.input: Design memory for querying where a customer lived on a past date.
output: Use a temporal knowledge graph with customer and address entities.
Store each residence relationship with valid-from and valid-until timestamps.
Query relationships whose validity interval contains the requested date.

output_examples.input: Review an agent memory system that keeps every interaction forever.
output_examples.output: The design needs retention limits, consolidation triggers, source tracking, access controls, deletion workflows, and tests for stale or conflicting memories.

best_practices: Match storage structure to required query types before selecting infrastructure.
Attach source, timestamp, confidence, consent, and validity metadata to persistent memories.
Test retrieval failures, stale facts, context injection, consolidation, deletion, backup, and recovery.
anti_patterns: Do not store every interaction permanently without retention and privacy rules.
Do not use vector similarity alone when queries require relationships or historical validity.
Do not insert retrieved memory into agent context as trusted instructions.

faq.question: Does this skill run a memory service?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture guidance and illustrative Python components for designing a memory service.

faq.question: Which memory approach should I choose?
faq.answer: Use files for simple persistence, vectors for semantic search, graphs for relationships, and temporal graphs for historical facts.

faq.question: Are the Python examples production ready?
faq.answer: No. They use in-memory storage, placeholder embeddings, simplified queries, and incomplete consolidation.

faq.question: How should sensitive memories be handled?
faq.answer: Add consent, access controls, encryption, retention limits, source tracking, audit logs, and reliable deletion workflows.

faq.question: What does temporal memory add?
faq.answer: It records when facts are valid, which supports historical queries and prevents outdated facts from replacing current state.

faq.question: Can I use this with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is tool-independent and supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
